chunks: Ali ibn al-Nu'man narrated from 'Amr ibn Shamar, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O people! By Allah, I surely know that you do not bring comfort to the people with your wealth, but rather with cheerfulness and good character.'
He (the narrator) said: And I heard him say: 'May Allah have mercy on every easy-going, cheerful one.'

key_terms.الطَّلَاقَةُ: Cheerfulness, affability, or ease of manner; the quality of being easy to get along with.
key_terms.حُسْنُ الْخُلُقِ: Good character or excellent moral conduct.
key_terms.سَهْلٍ طَلْقٍ: Easy-going and cheerful; a compound phrase describing a person who is gentle and affable.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between bringing comfort through wealth and through character according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, the Prophet (SAWW) distinguishes between material provision and social ease, emphasizing that 'al-tilaqah' (cheerfulness and affability) is the key to making people feel comfortable. This aligns with the Shia scholarly emphasis on *husn al-khuluq* as a practical manifestation of faith, where emotional accessibility is valued as highly as financial generosity. The concluding supplication highlights the spiritual merit of maintaining a gentle, approachable demeanor in daily interactions.
